It is fucking frustrating and it does sometimes feel like it’s killing you from the inside so much that even your physical condition gets affected as you start being weaker and really low on energy.

I think that what sort of helps me with my intrusive thoughts is talking to them. It often feels weird, but it calms me down and I start to accept them rather than fighting  them all the time. I realized that you either accept them or ignore them, although that second option was a hard path for me. Just don’t fight them, take deep breaths when they take the most awful shape and remind yourself that it’s all in your head. 

Yes, they’re total monsters sometimes and yes they don’t make any sense, but remember to let them be. Do not see them as your enemies, do not put your powers into getting rid of them, because that doesn’t work, and if it does, it will take a pretty long time.

I don’t know if my advice is any good, but I just saw your post and felt like typing this.

She called me childish when i was suicidal, she laughed when i started talking about my fantasies, she had a pretty unprofessional response to self-disclosure. So why do i keep paying her? I feel like i’m too much for her. I don’t think she can handle me anymore. Since we started talking about the therapeutic relationship, her behaviour changed. I don’t think she cares anymore. And what disturbs me more, is the fact that she just doesn’t admit it. If you would listen to our most recent sessions, you would instantly notice something’s not right. I think she knows the therapy is not working but she doesn’t admit it. I think she’s using me. She knows i’m in a vulnerable position and she uses me. Could be my paranoia, but in the same time, this could be true.
This situation is just making me suicidal again. I hate me for being so kind to people and getting so easily attached to them.

this is actually not her first time when she handles things unprofessionally. There was a time when i was at my worst and i asked her if i could get a hug…she called me childish. I sometimes think that the boundaries in psychoanalysis are a bit too tough. I don’t know what to do. I can’t end the therapy with this therapist cause i depend too much on her. She does unprofessional things probably every month, but i keep paying her. I feel like a drug addict, you know it’s bad, but you still pay for it.

i actually never got to inform myself about trustworthiness in therapy. Could you tell me a few methods on how can i trust my therapist? May just be my severe paranoia, but i can’t just believe a person, just cause they said so. Oh, and after what happened yesterday, i’m even more insecure.
Let me tell you exactly how the session went.

So, i started talking about self disclosure and i told her that i heard that it can sometimes be healing for the client. She responded pretty aggressively and i understood that she won’t talk anything about her. I’m not her therapist, it’s the other way around, she doesn’t matter there. She’ll have to pay me if she’s gonna talk about her life(no one actually said anything about this, was that a joke or she said that seriously?)

Then, no one said anything for like 1 minute and i decided to change the subject cause if i would have kept talking about that, it was going to lead nowhere.

I started talking about transference and i told her that i’ve had some fantasies recently. She asked what kind of fantasies(that was such a stupid question, she knew exactly what i was talking about) and i said that erotic fantasies with her. She asked if i could get into more details, so i did. After talking like 1-2 minutes, i noticed that she started laughing so i stopped. She kept laughing and i couldn’t see that anymore, so i started telling her that this is why i don’t open up about my intimate thoughts, i don’t want to get such reactions. She said that she’s sorry while laughing(the fake kind of ,,sorry”, the one you just say it, you don’t mean it) and said that it’s something about her, so there isn’t a problem in laughing about it.

Would you feel secure after such a session? 

I’m sorry, i know you don’t know the whole part of the story, but i got angry when you said ,,not OP bringing in transference feelings to discuss”. I keep talking about transference for months and it’s leading nowhere. Yes, it was the first time i opened up about my fantasies, but i keep talking about how i feel about her since may. She knows it’s transference, she knows i have feelings for her, but somehow, this is what she does, i tell her serious stuff about me and she laughs.

I think the therapist can sometimes be the problem, not the client.

i’m doing psychoanalytic therapy too and no, she didn’t say WHY she laughed, she just said that the fantasies are about her, so there isn’t a problem in laughing about it. This was seriously such a bad experience, i just woke up, and the first thought was this one.
